Central Station,
Date March 10, 19 32.

Subject (in full) Commercial Press temporary office, 78 Szechuen Road. Information.

Made by C. D. I. MacDermott. Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,
C.D.S. 86 reports that at 3:30 p.m. 10-3-32 the five ex-workers (with same spokesman) mentioned in my report of 9-3-32 again visited the above office for relief.
They were told by Mr. Y. . Wong ( Wong Yuin Foo I : 2 ) to call again on 12-3-32 at 3 p.m. when something definite might be told them. It is impossible to make any definite decision until the conference of the Company's Directors is ended.
It appears these five ex-workers were selected to represent all the ex-workers (about 3,000) of the various Departments in discussions with the Company, as to what treatment they (ex-workers) were to receive. The spokesman (Yung Tsang Faung) asked for $20.00 for each ex-worker, this amount to be deducted from any wages they may earn from the Company in the future, or from any monies which may be standing in the company to the credit of the ex-workers under the bonus system in vogue prior to the destruction of the company's premises in Chapei.
There are at present only about 200 ex-workers in Shanghai and they have a small office in Room 19 of the Sungkiang (中 : 2 ) lodging house, 88 Hankow Road.

(批：Received 11/3/32 [Signature])

Yours obediently
[Signature]
C. D. I.

D. D. O. "A"
Officer i/c O. C. Special Branch.

先生：
华探第86号报告称，1932年3月10日下午3时30分，我在1932年3月9日报告中提及的五名前雇员（同一发言人）再次前往上述办事处寻求救济。
王云五先生（Wong Yuin Foo I : 2）告知他们于1932年3月12日下午3时再来，届时可能会告知他们确切消息。在公司董事会议结束之前，不可能做出任何确切决定。
看来这五名前雇员是被选出来代表各部门所有前雇员（约3,000人）与公司进行谈判，商讨他们（前雇员）将受到何种待遇。发言人（Yung Tsang Faung）要求为每名前雇员发放20.00美元，该金额将从他们未来从公司获得的工资中扣除，或从闸北公司 premises 被毁前流行的奖金制度下记在前雇员贷方的任何款项中扣除。
目前在上海的前雇员仅约200人，他们在汉口路88号松江（中 : 2）旅馆19室有一个小办公室。

（批注：1932年3月11日收到 [签名]）

敬礼
[签名]
C. D. I.

File No. ______
Central Station,
Date March 8, 1932.

Subject (in full) Report on Chinese refugees in Central District.

Made by C. D. I. MacDermott. Forwarded by Jas. S. Adams
C.I.

Sir,

I beg to report that the number of Chinese refugees living
in Central District on 7-3-32 was approximately 6,376. This is
a decrease of 1608 on the previous day's figures. The decrease is
mainly due to a number of refugees returning to their homes in
Hongkew, Yangtsepoo and Chapei and leaving Shanghai for Canton,
Ningpo, Wusih, and Kompo by boats and steamers via Soochow Creek
and Whangpoo River.

6,000 Cantonese refugees from the Zang-chow Guild, 2 Chengtu
Road; Wah-veh-z (temple) (活佛寺), Tatung Road; the Chinese Y.M.C.A.
Szechuen Road, and the Shanghai Commercial Savings Bank building,
were repatriated to Canton under the auspices of the Cantonese
Relief Association by the "S.S. Hwa Tung" on 7-3-32. The ship sails
on 8-3-32.

I am, Sir,

Yours obediently,

C. D. I. MacDermott

C. D. I.

Officer i/c Special Branch.

事由（全称）：中区中国难民报告。

呈报人：C. D. I. MacDermott。转呈人：Jas. S. Adams
C.I.

先生：

谨报告称，1932年3月7日居住在中区的中国难民人数约为6,376人。较前一日数字减少1,608人。减少的主要原因是部分难民返回虹口、杨树浦和闸北的家园，以及经由苏州河和黄浦江乘船和轮船离开上海前往广州、宁波、无锡和Kompo（音译）。

1932年3月7日，在成都路2号潮州会馆、大通路活佛寺（Wah-veh-z）、四川路中华基督教青年会以及上海商业储蓄银行大楼的6,000名广东籍难民，在广东救济协会的主持下，由“华东轮”（S.S. Hwa Tung）遣返广州。该船于1932年3月8日启航。

此致，

敬礼，

C. D. I. MacDermott

C. D. I.

特别课主管警官。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No. 67/32.

REPORT
Central Station,
Date March 3, 19 32.

Subject (in full) Report on an infernal machine found at 65 Peking Road.

Made by D. S. Pryde. Forwarded by Jos. H. Adams c-l

Sir,
At 4:15 p.m. 3-3-32 Mr. Bothelo (Portugese) reported that he had found what he believed to be a bomb in a case of lard stored in his godown at 65 Peking Road. Mr. Bothelo had removed a cargo of this lard from a godown in Chapei. D. S.s Pryde and Taylor attended and after viewing the supposed bomb obtained the assistance of Mr. Sutcliff (an authority on infernal machines) from Mustard & Company. Mr. Sutcliff was of the opinion that it was an unexploded Japanese aerial bomb and placed it in a bath of water. Mr. Sutcliff considered the machine was dangerous.
The Japanese authorities were informed and a Japanese Naval Officer attended and stated it was a Chinese mortar shell with the fins missing. He also was of the opinion it was dangerous and as it was Chinese the Japanese would not remove it. This infernal machine has been left in water in the godown and the door of which is locked and no person allowed to enter. Judging by other Chinese mortar shells seen, the Japanese opinion that it is one of these with the fins missing appears to be probably correct.

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently,
Geo. B. Pryde
D. S. 101.

[Signature] 4/3
Senior Detective (Central).

Officer i/c Special Branch.

主题（全称）关于在北京路65号发现爆炸装置的报告。

由 D. S. Pryde 撰写。由 Jos. H. Adams c-l 转呈

先生：
1932年3月3日下午4时15分，博特洛先生（葡萄牙人）报告称，他在北京路65号的仓库内储存的一箱猪油中发现了他认为是炸弹的物品。博特洛先生将这批猪油从闸北的一个仓库运出。D. S. Pryde 和 Taylor 到场，在查看该疑似炸弹后，请来了 Mustard & Company 公司的萨克利夫先生（爆炸装置专家）协助。萨克利夫先生认为这是一枚未爆炸的日本航空炸弹，并将其放入一缸水中。萨克利夫先生认为该装置具有危险性。
已通知日本当局，一名日本海军军官到场并称这是一枚尾翼缺失的中国迫击炮弹。他也认为其具有危险性，并因系中国制造，日方不予移除。该爆炸装置已被留在仓库的水中，仓库门已上锁，禁止任何人进入。根据所见其他中国迫击炮弹判断，日方认为这是尾翼缺失的迫击炮弹的观点似乎是正确的。

此致，
敬礼，
Geo. B. Pryde
D. S. 101.

[签名] 3月4日
高级侦探（中央）。

特别分部主管警官。

Subject (in full) Report on Chinese refugees in Central District.

Made by C. D. I. MacDermott. Forwarded by ____________________

Sir,

I beg to report that the number of Chinese refugees living
in Central District on 2-3-32 was approximately 2,613. This is
a decrease of 94 on the previous day's figures. The decrease is
mainly due to a number of refugees leaving Shanghai for Ningpo,
Hongkong, Canton, Nanking, Wuchow and Hangchow by boats and
steamers via Soochow Creek and Yangpoo River.

1425 Cantonese deck passengers left by "S.S. Tolo", these
persons personally paid $20.00 each for their passages which were
booked by the China Travel Service.

Refugees
3/3/32

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently,
C. D. I. MacDermott

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.

File No.______

Central Station,
Date March 2, 19 32.

REPORT

Subject (in full) Wounded soldiers in Central District.

Made by C. D. I. MacDermott. Forwarded by ____________________

Sir,

6 wounded soldiers from Chapei were admitted to the Swastika Hospital, 24 Ningpo Road on 1-3-32. This makes a total of 90 now in the hospital.

A branch Red Cross hospital, 202 Shantung Road (35th Red Cross) received 40 wounded soldiers from Chapei on 1-3-32 on which date the hospital opened. This hospital can accomodate 150 patients.

Another hospital for wounded soldiers was opened on 1-3-32 under the auspices of the Shanghai Ladies (Chinese) Association (Madame Chiang Kai Zah ) for wounded soldiers at 38 Kiukiang Road. 11 wounded soldiers from Chapei were admitted on 1-3-32. This hospital can accomodate 800 wounded. On 2-3-32 a further 169 wounded were admitted (total 180). The Doctor i/c is one Lieu Zai Ung. (刘瑞恒).

I am, Sir,

Yours obediently,
C. D. I. MacDermott.

C. D. I.

Officer i/c Special Branch.

中央捕房，
日期 1932年3月2日。

报告

事由（全称） 中区伤兵情况。

呈报人 C. D. I. MacDermott。 转呈人 ____________________

先生，

6名来自闸北的伤兵于1932年3月1日被送入宁波路24号红卍字会医院。这使得该院目前的伤兵总数达到90人。

位于山东路202号的红十字会分院（第三十五红十字会）于1932年3月1日开院，当日接收了40名来自闸北的伤兵。该医院可容纳150名病人。

另一所伤兵医院于1932年3月1日在上海妇女（中国）协会（蒋夫人）的主持下在九江路38号开设，专门收治伤兵。1932年3月1日接收了11名来自闸北的伤兵。该医院可容纳800名伤兵。1932年3月2日又接收了169名伤兵（总计180人）。负责医生为刘瑞恒（Lieu Zai Ung）。

此致，

敬礼，
C. D. I. MacDermott。

C. D. I.

特别课主管警官。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.

File No. 63/32.

REPORT

Central Station,
Date February 26, 1932.

Subject (in full) Male Chinese wounded by stray bullet.

Made by D. S. I. Shields. Forwarded by Jno L. Adams.

Sir,

I beg to report that at 5 p.m. 26-2-32 C.P.C. 1849 who was
on duty on Honan Road near Peking Road brought to this Station
a male Chinese named Woo Kyi Woh (吳其華), age 15, native of
Ningpo and residing at No. 1 North Soochow Road and reported that
while patrolling above Road he was approached by the above men-
tioned boy who stated that while he was walking South to North on
Honan Road near Peking Road he felt something strike him on the
right thigh, he was seen to be bleeding so the C.P.C. took him to
the Lester Chinese Hospital where he was examined by Dr. Ho. It
was then found that he was suffering from a bullet wound which
went half through the thigh, not serious, will require about 10
days treatment as an outdoor patient. When questioned both the
C.P.C. and the wounded man state that they never heard any report
of a rifle being discharged it is thought that this is a stray
bullet from the direction of Chapel. The injured man proceeded
to his home.

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently,
J. Shields.
D. S. I.

(Signed)
Senior Detective (Central).

Officer i/c Special Branch.

报告

中央捕房，
日期：1932年2月26日。

事由（全称）：一名华籍男子被流弹击伤。

呈报人：副巡官希尔德斯 (D. S. I. Shields)。转呈人：约翰·L·亚当斯 (Jno L. Adams)。

阁下：

谨此报告，1932年2月26日下午5时，在河南路近北京路一带执勤的华籍警长第1849号将一名名为吴其华 (Woo Kyi Woh) 的华籍男子带至本捕房。该男子15岁，宁波人，居住于苏州路北首1号。据报，上述警长在巡逻上述路段时，该男孩上前称，当他在河南路近北京路处由南向北行走时，感觉右大腿被某物击中。因其可见出血，该华籍警长遂将其送往莱斯医院 (Lester Chinese Hospital)，由何医生 (Dr. Ho) 进行检查。检查发现其遭受枪伤，子弹射入大腿一半深度，伤势不重，需作为门诊病人治疗约10天。经询问，该华籍警长及伤者均表示未听到任何步枪射击声。推测此系来自闸北 (Chapel) 方向的流弹。伤者已返回家中。

此致，
敬礼

J. 希尔德斯。
副巡官。

（签名）
高级侦探（中央）。

特别课主管警官。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No. 62/32.
Central Station,
REPORT
Date February 25, 1932.
Subject (in full) Gathering of labourers etc. at 66 Szechuen Road.
Made by D. S. I. Shields. Forwarded by Jas. L. Ceamans
C.I.

Sir,
I beg to report that at 10:55 a.m. 25-2-32 a telephone
message was received from the Shanghai Citizens Emergency Committee
Relief Division at 66 Szechuen Road to the effect that a large
number of ex-mill workers of the Japanese mills and students had
gathered at the above address and were demanding relief in the
form of food and that they refused to disperse.
A party of Police proceeded to the scene and there ascertained
that about 400 male and female mill workers and students had
congregated and were demanding food. It was explained to them by
the above Relief Committee that they were there only for the
relief of refugees and that the labour and student class would
get their relief from the Social Bureau, 4 Avenue Joffre in the
French Concession to whom the above committee had granted 600
piculs of rice.
They refused to accept this explanation and were persistent
in their demand for food whereupon they were ejected by the Police,
they then dispersed in an orderly manner. The names of the
student representatives are as follows:-
Tsai Yue Tsang (蔡月章) on the Resident Committee of the
Yih Dah Middle School, 476 Avenue Haig. Tsung Sih Hai and Tse
Vah Liang (程雪海及施維良) from the Anhwei Middle School, Chapei.
These men and several female students were brought to this
Station for enquiries to see if any underlying motive was behind
their demand but on it being determined that there was not, they
were released.

(批：K.R 26/2/32 32)

Tuson.
Senior Detective (Central).
Officer i/c O. C. Special Branch.

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently,
D. S. I. Shields

阁下：

谨此报告，1932年2月25日上午10时55分，接到四川路66号上海市民紧急委员会救济部的电话消息，称大量日资纱厂的前工人和学生聚集在上述地址，要求以食物形式提供救济，并拒绝解散。

一队警察前往现场，经查实，约有400名男女纱厂工人和学生聚集，并要求提供食物。上述救济委员会向他们解释，该处仅用于救济难民，劳工和学生阶层应从法租界霞飞路4号的社会局获得救济，上述委员会已向该局拨付600担大米。

他们拒绝接受这一解释，坚持要求提供食物，随后被警察驱逐，之后有序散去。学生代表姓名如下：
蔡月章 (Tsai Yue Tsang)，海格路476号义达中学住校委员会成员。程雪海 (Tsung Sih Hai) 及施维良 (Tse Vah Liang)，来自闸北安徽中学。
这些人及几名女学生被带至本捕房进行讯问，以查明其要求背后是否有潜在动机，但在确定并无此类动机后，予以释放。

（批注：K.R 1932年2月26日 32）

图森 (Tuson)。
高级侦探（中央）。
特别课主管警官。

此致，
敬礼

副巡官 希尔德斯

Subject (in full) Stray bullet inside the premises of Bank de l' Indo-Chine.

Made by D. S. Satula Forwarded by Jas. G. Geary C.I.

(批：Semilo P.D.O.N)
(批：Recorded)

Sir,
With reference to the attached letter the undersigned visited the above Bank and interviewed assistant manager, Mr. P. Olry.
It was ascertained that between the 29-1-32 and the 15-2-32 about ten stray bullets hit the Northern wall of the building. No notice was taken of same till 12:10 p.m. 15-2-32 when a bullet coming from the North-Western direction, probably the Railway Station, broke a big pane of glass in a window facing North and passing close to a Chinese accountant hit the blotting pad on his desk.
At present the Bank authorities are taking precautions against the stray bullets that may possibly come their way by barricading all the windows on the North side with iron sheets about ¼" thick.

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently,

(签名：Jasatula)

(签名：Theson.)

Subject (in full) Report on shell bursting behind the Palace Hotel.

Made by D. S. Beloshenko Forwarded by J. A. Adams
C. I.

Sir,
At 11:20 a.m. 13-2-32 S.P.W. 758 employed at the Palace Hotel
came to the Station and reported an explosion in the compound of the
Palace Hotel.
From enquiries made it was learned that a small shell had
dropped on the corrugated iron sheet roof of the watchman's hut
at the rear of the Palace Hotel.
The shell, which must have been a very small one, probably
was fired from an anti-aircraft gun and dropped straight down.
By the marks left, it appears to have been similar to the
shell bursting behind the Shanghai Club on the 11-2-32.
No one injured. The only damage is a hole in the roof and
two broken panes of glass in a first floor window.

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently,

D. S. Beloshenko
D. S. 211.

Mason.
Senior Detective (Central).

Subject (in full) Extract from Occurrence Book.

Made by C. D. I. Mason. Forwarded by Jas. H. Adams
C. I.

Sir,
At 5:30 p.m. 12-2-32 Special Police Sgt. 72, Mutkin and
S. P. Const. 88 Bohokoff reported that whilst coming off duty at
4:45 p.m. they observed a Chinese coolie collapse on Soochow
Road and on enquiring discovered he had been wounded. They
immediately removed him to the General Hospital for treatment and
later to the Lester Chinese Hospital, where he was detained.
C.D.C. 147 made enquiries at the above named Hospital and learned
from the wounded man that his name is Lee Ah Foh, office coolie,
employed by the Centrosogus England Company Ltd., 2 Peking Road,
and residing 486 Haining Road, and after delivering letters to
the Chinese Post office, North Szechuen Road, crossed the bridge
into Soochow Road and when at Soochow and Yuen Ming Yuen Roads
corner, was wounded by a stray bullet which wounded him in the
chest. Doctors Chit is as follows:-
"Bullet wound through chest. The injury is fairly serious,
detained in Hospital for treatment."

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently,
Mason.
Officer i/c O. C. Special Branch. C. D. I.

先生：
1932年2月12日下午5时30分，特别巡捕警士72号 Mutkin 和特别巡捕警员88号 Bohokoff 报告称，他们在下午4时45分下班途中，观察到一名华籍苦力在苏州路倒地，经询问发现其受伤。他们立即将其送往公济医院（General Hospital）接受治疗，随后转往莱斯特华人医院（Lester Chinese Hospital），该人在该院留院治疗。
中央侦探课147号在上述医院进行调查，并从伤者处获悉，其名为 Lee Ah Foh（音译：李阿福），职业为办公苦力，受雇于北京路2号的 Centrosogus England Company Ltd.（原文如此），居住在海宁路486号。他在向北四川路的中国邮局投递信件后，过桥进入苏州路，当行至苏州路与圆明园路转角处时，被一发流弹击中胸部受伤。医生诊断如下：
“胸部贯穿枪伤。伤势相当严重，留院治疗。”

此致，
敬礼，
Mason.

Central Station,

Date February 12, 1932.

Subject (in full) Report on shell bursting behind the Shanghai Club.

Made by D. S. Beloshenko Forwarded by Jas. L. Adams

（批：Recorded）

Sir,
At 11 a.m. 11-2-32 C.S.I. Chu when on duty at the corner of Avenue Edward VII and The Bund heard an explosion from the direction of Canton Road. He was unable to locate the scene of the explosion until after 4 p.m. 11-2-32 when he learned that a small shell had dropped at the rear of the Shanghai Club in an alleyway between the S.P.C. sub-station and MacKenzie & Company's godown. A private watchman named Tsu Sai Huh, age 67, employed by MacKenzie & Co., who was in the vicinity at the time, was very slightly injured in the right arm by fragments. He was not located till 9:30 a.m. 12-2-32.

The shell, which must have been a very small one, appears to have been fired at aircraft and expended its self and dropped straight down. Apart from injuring the watchman and cracking a window of MacKenzie & Co.'s godown, no other damage was done.

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently,

(Signature)
Senior Detective (Central) f.
D. S. 211.

Officer i/c Special Branch.

（批注：已归档）

先生：
1932年2月11日上午11时，华籍探员 Chu 在爱多亚路（Avenue Edward VII）与外滩转角处执勤时，听到来自广东路方向的爆炸声。他无法确定爆炸地点，直到1932年2月11日下午4时后才获悉，一枚小炮弹落在上海总会后方，位于工部局警务处分站与麦肯锡公司（MacKenzie & Company）仓库之间的一条小巷内。当时在该附近的一名受雇于麦肯锡公司的私人看守 Tsu Sai Huh（音译：朱赛虎？），67岁，右臂被碎片轻微炸伤。直到1932年2月12日上午9时30分才找到他。

这枚炮弹肯定非常小，似乎是向飞机射击后耗尽动能垂直落下。除致使看守受伤及震裂麦肯锡公司仓库的一扇窗户外，未造成其他损害。

此致，
敬礼，

高级侦探（中央）代
D. S. 211.

Date February 9, 19 32.

Subject (in full) Window of N.K.K. Building damaged by several stray bullets.

Made by J. D. S. I. Nakamura. Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,
At 10:30 a.m. 9-2-32 Mr. J. Shiozawa, representative of
Nisshin Kisen Kaisha, No. 5 The Bund, came to this Station and
reported that about 9:30 a.m. a window on the 4th floor of the
N.K.K. building was smashed by bullets.
From enquiries made by D.S.I. Nakamura the following was
ascertained:- At about 9:30 a.m. to-day whilst two Chinese
coolies were cleaning a passage on the 4th floor of the building,
they heard a big noise at a passage window which is situated at
the back of the building and facing West, and found 7 bullet
holes in the window glass. They then immediately reported the
matter to the office.
From further enquiries made by D.S.I. Nakamura it was
found that there were 10 bullets marks on the wall very near to
the said window, but D.S.I. Nakamura could not find any bullets.
According to the circumstances the window was damaged by stray
bullets. No one injured and nothing damaged except window glass.

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently,

J. D. S. I.
[Signature]
Senior Detective (Central).

Officer i/c Special Branch.

先生：
1932年2月9日上午10时30分，外滩5号日清汽船会社（Nisshin Kisen Kaisha）代表 J. Shiozawa 先生来到本捕房报告称，当日上午9时30分左右，日清汽船会社（N.K.K.）大楼四楼的一扇窗户被子弹击碎。
经警佐中村（D.S.I. Nakamura）查询，查明情况如下：今日上午9时30分左右，两名中国苦力正在该大楼四楼的一条通道上打扫时，听到位于大楼背面、朝西的通道窗户处传来一声巨响，发现窗玻璃上有7个弹孔。他们随即立即向办事处报告此事。
经警佐中村进一步查询，发现在靠近上述窗户的墙上有10处弹痕，但警佐中村未能找到任何子弹。根据现场情况判断，窗户系被流弹击毁。除窗玻璃外，无人受伤，亦无其他财物受损。

此致，
敬礼，

J. D. S. I.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
Central Station,
REPORT
Date February 6, 1932.

Subject (in full) Two Japanese assaulted by a mob of Chinese on Peking Road.
(Hongkew District)

Made by J. D. S. I. Nakamura Forwarded by Jash. Adams.

Sir,
With reference to the above at 3 p.m. to-day, D.S.I. Nakamura proceeded to the Hospital and the victims were interviewed.
From further enquiries made it was ascertained that at 12 noon 5-2-32 M. Ogata and K. Yuki visited a certain Chinese house at Nanking Road for their own business. At 1:30 p.m. on their way back to their homes, whilst they were walking along Peking Road near the new market (near road unknown) several Chinese suddenly came from behind and assaulted them. M. Ogata saw a number of Foreign Volunteers were piling sand bags on the road, so he immediately went and asked their help. Two said volunteers were accompanied by him and came to the scene. When they ran up to the spot, K. Yuki was already unconscious and lying on the road and he was surrounded by a crowd of people. In the meantime M. Ogata was also assaulted by them with stones and other weapons and fell down. He could not remember after that and when M. Ogata recovered from unconsciousness he was taken to the Hospital in a motor truck (which belonged to the Haigai Wata Kaisha) by a Japanese named Mr. Matsumura, Haigai Wata Kaisha.
Dr. Sugamma of the Hospital was interviewed and stated that the first victim named K. Yuki's condition was very serious, at least it will take about six months treatment to be cured completely. The second victim named M. Ogata's wound was not much serious, takes about a month to be cured.

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently,
(Signature)
Senior Detective (Central). (Signature)
J. D. S. I.
Officer i/c Special Branch.

日期 1932年2月6日。

主题（全称） 两名日本人在北京路被一群中国人殴打。（虹口区）

制作人 日籍高级警探 (J. D. S. I.) 中村 (Nakamura) 转呈人 贾什·亚当斯 (Jash. Adams)。

先生，
关于上述事项，今日下午3时，日籍高级警探中村前往医院，并对受害者进行了问话。
经进一步查询，查明1932年2月5日中午12时，绪方氏 (M. Ogata) 和雪木氏 (K. Yuki) 因私事前往南京路某中国房屋。下午1时30分，在返回住所途中，当他们沿北京路靠近新市场（附近道路不详）行走时，几名中国人突然从背后袭来并殴打他们。绪方氏看到一些外国志愿人员正在路上堆砌沙袋，便立即前去求助。两名志愿人员随他一同来到现场。当他们赶到现场时，雪木氏已不省人事，躺在路上，周围围着一群人。与此同时，绪方氏也遭到他们用石块和其他武器袭击并倒地。此后他便失去记忆，当绪方氏从昏迷中苏醒时，已被一名名为松村氏 (Mr. Matsumura) 的日本人（海盖瓦塔会社 (Haigai Wata Kaisha) 职员）用一辆卡车（属于海盖瓦塔会社）送往医院。
经询问医院杉山医生 (Dr. Sugamma)，他表示第一名受害者雪木氏 (K. Yuki) 的伤势非常严重，完全治愈至少需要约六个月的治疗时间。第二名受害者绪方氏 (M. Ogata) 的伤势不太严重，约需一个月即可痊愈。

此致，
敬礼，
（签名）
高级警探（中央）。 （签名）
日籍高级警探 (J. D. S. I.)
特别课主管警官。

Central Station,

Date February 5, 19 32.

Subject (in full) Two Japanese being assaulted by a mob of Chinese at Peking and
Fokien Roads corner.

Made by J.D.S.I. Nakamura Forwarded by Jas. G. Adams
C.I.

Sir,
With reference to the above D.S.I. Nakamura was instructed
by C.D.I. Mason to make enquiries.
At 8:30 p.m. on the 5-2-32, D.S.I. Nakamura proceeded to the
Japanese hospital, 68 Boone Road and saw two Japanese who were
unable to speak as they were in a very serious condition.
The wives of the victims who were in the hospital stated that
the names of the victims were K. Yuki and N. Ogata residing at 12
and 12A Woosung Road respectively and they were both employed by
Eastern Ice Manufacturing Company, 521 Chining Road.
At 9 a.m. to-day they left their homes together without say-
ing where they were going and at 2:30 p.m. they (the wives) were
informed of the assault by the hospital authorities. The wives
immediately visited them at the hospital and were informed by the
second victim named N. Ogata that at 1:30 p.m. to-day whilst they
were proceeding in ricshas on Peking Road near Fokien Road they
were stopped by a mob of Chinese and assaulted by them with stones
and other weapons. They could not remember after that as they
were rendered unconscious.
D.S.I. Nakamura could not obtain further results to enqui-
ries other than the particulars contained in the Occurrence Book
at Louza Station which states that at about 1:30 p.m. five Japan-
ese males were riding in ricshas on Peking Road when they were
attacked by a crowd of Chinese..
On visiting the hospital where the two injured men are now
detained no information could be obtained other than that they
are both suffering from serious head wounds.
A further visit will be paid to the hospital on 6-2-32.

(Signed)
Mason.
Senior Detective (Central)
J. D. S. I.

日期 1932年2月5日。

主题（全称） 两名日本人在北京路与福建路转角处被一群中国人殴打。

制作人 日籍高级警探 (J.D.S.I.) 中村 (Nakamura) 转呈人 贾斯·G·亚当斯 (Jas. G. Adams)
巡官 (C.I.)

先生，
关于上述事项，日籍高级警探中村奉首席督察梅森之命进行调查。
1932年2月5日晚上8时30分，日籍高级警探中村前往布恩路68号的日本医院，看望了两名日本人，因他们病情危重，无法言语。
在医院里的受害者妻子称，受害者姓名为雪木氏 (K. Yuki) 和小田氏 (N. Ogata) [注：此处原文为N. Ogata，前文为M. Ogata]，分别居住在吴淞路12号和12A号，两人均受雇于济宁路521号的东方制冰公司。
今天上午9时，他们一起离家，未告知去向；下午2时30分，她们（妻子们）接到医院当局通知，得知了殴打事件。妻子们立即前往医院探望，并从第二名受害者小田氏 (N. Ogata) 处获悉，今天下午1时30分，当他们乘坐人力车沿北京路靠近福建路行驶时，被一群中国人拦下，并用石块和其他武器殴打他们。此后他们因昏迷而不省人事，无法回忆后续情况。
除老闸捕房记事簿中记载的内容外，日籍高级警探中村未能通过调查获得更多结果，记事簿称下午1时30分左右，五名日本男子在北京路乘坐人力车时遭到一群中国人的袭击。
在探访目前扣留两名伤者的医院时，除得知两人均头部受重伤外，未获得其他信息。
将于1932年2月6日再次前往医院探访。

（签名）
梅森 (Mason)。
高级警探（中央）
日籍高级警探 (J. D. S. I.)

REPORT

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
& S. B. REGISTRY
S. B. D. 3157
Central Station,
2 / 1. 32.
Date January 31, 1932.

Subject (in full) Armed Japanese in Cathay Hotel.

Made by D. S. Darvill Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,
At 1:40 p.m. on the 31-1-32 Mr. Telfer, manager of the Cathay
Hotel, telephoned that an armed Japanese patrol had entered the
hotel.
C.D.I. Mason, S.I.s Tullock and Hutton, D. S. Taylor and the
undersigned proceeded to the Cathay Hotel and learned from the
manager, that armed Japanese were in room No. 500. An immediate
visit to this room however found that they had departed and had
probably passed down in a lift, whilst the Police were ascending.
Enquiries show that Room No. 500 was occupied by one named Lee
Shai Htone, general manager of the Tiger Medical Company, 1337
North Szechuen Road and his two nieces. Mr. Lee informed the
Police that he was a British born subject having been born and
raised in Burma. He came to Shanghai two years before and had
carried on business at 1337 North Szechuen Road.
At about 9 a.m. on the 31-1-32, he and his family were in
the house, when a party of Japanese marines and plain clothes
volunteers wearing red and white arm bands, forced their way into
his house by way of the roof and coming to the room occupied by
Mr. Lee and his family, ordered him to unlock the door. As this
order was not instantly complied with a shot was fired through
the door by the intruders, which wounded a Chinese servant in the
left wrist. Mr. Lee then immediately opened the door, and he was
confronted by the Japanese who told him that they were under
orders to shoot or capture all inmates of the house. Mr. Lee in-
formed them that he was a British subject, whereupon he was
allowed to obtain his valuables and at about 10 a.m. he and his
nieces were escorted to the Cathay Hotel by four armed Japanese
plain clothes volunteers. Upon booking Room No. 500, he was taken

（批：Perusal H.P. 1/2）

上海公共租界工部局警务处

中央捕房，
1932年1月2日。
日期：1932年1月31日。

事由（全称）：华懋饭店内的武装日本人。

制作人：D. S. Darvill 转呈人：[签名]

先生：

1932年1月31日下午1时40分，华懋饭店（Cathay Hotel）经理泰尔弗（Telfer）先生致电称，一支武装日本巡逻队已进入该饭店。

刑事侦缉督察梅森（Mason）、警佐塔洛克（Tullock）和赫顿（Hutton）、侦探长泰勒（Taylor）以及卑职随即前往华懋饭店，并从经理处获悉，武装日本人位于500号房间。然而，立即对该房间进行的搜查发现，他们已离开，很可能在警察上楼时乘电梯下楼离去。

经查，500号房间由一名名为李载东（Lee Shai Htone，音译）的人士及其两名侄女占用。李先生是虎标医药公司（Tiger Medical Company）的总经理，公司地址位于四川北路1337号。李先生告知警方，他是出生于缅甸并在当地长大的英国籍臣民。他于两年前来到上海，一直在四川北路1337号经商。

1932年1月31日上午9时许，他和家人正在家中，此时一群佩戴红白臂章的日本海军陆战队士兵及便衣义勇队员通过屋顶强行闯入其住宅，来到李先生及其家人所在的房间，命令他开门。由于未立即服从该命令，闯入者向门内开了一枪，击中一名中国仆人的左手腕。李先生随即立即打开房门，面对日本人，对方告知他，他们奉命射杀或俘获屋内所有人员。李先生表明自己是英国臣民，随后获准取走其贵重物品。上午10时许，他和他的侄女们在四名武装日本便衣义勇队员的护送下被带至华懋饭店。在办理500号房间入住手续后，他被护送人员带往

（批注：阅毕 H.P. 1/2）

there by the escort. Mr. Lee then desired knowledge of the where-
abouts of his nephew Lee Chong Moh aged 21, and his wounded ser-
vant, who had been taken away when the house was raided. Mr. Lee
explained to the Japanese Volunteers that his nephew was also a
British born subject and that he desired his release or assurances
of his safety. The volunteers then left the room and proceeded
to leave the Hotel but they were accosted in the Lobby by Mr. E. Negri,
(in)
general manager, who demanded to know why they were on the premi-
ses armed. They gave no answer to him and left the Hotel.
At about 1:15 p.m. even date, he was informed that the volun-
teers had returned to Mr. Lee's room and he proceeded there and
observed that 3 of them were armed with pistols and one with a
rifle. After he had received Mr. Lee's assurances that the Japan-
ese were there with his permission, Mr. Negri left but telephoned
to the Police. As previously stated, the Japanese had left the
Hotel by the time the Police arrived but Mr. Lee was interrogated
and he admitted that on the second visit he had been informed by
the volunteers that his nephew's life was in danger, but that
everything would be done by them to secure his release. Mr. Lee
then states that partly because he himself was escorted safely to
the Hotel by the volunteers and because of their promise to effect
the release of his nephew he gave to them $600.00, and they de-
parted assuring him that they would probably be able to effect
the release of the nephew on the next day (1-2-32).
Further questioning resulted in finding that Mr. Lee and his
nephew were born in Burma and claimed British nationality but that
in 1929, when coming to Shanghai they had taken out Chinese pass-
ports and had no British passports in their possession, nor were
they registered at the H.B.M. Consulate in Shanghai.

那里。随后，李先生希望得知其21岁的侄子李仲模（Lee Chong Moh，音译）及在住宅遭突袭时被带走的受伤仆人的下落。李先生向日本义勇队员解释称，其侄子也是出生于缅甸的英国臣民，他希望将其释放或保证其安全。义勇队员随后离开房间并准备离开饭店，但在大堂被总经理内格里（E. Negri）先生拦住，内格里先生质问他们为何武装出现在该场所。他们未作回答便离开了饭店。

同日约下午1时15分，有人告知李先生，义勇队员已返回其房间，内格里先生随即前往该处，观察到其中三人持有手枪，一人持有步枪。在得到李先生保证日本人是经其允许留在该处后，内格里先生离开，但随即打电话通知警方。如前所述，警察到达时日本人已离开饭店，但警方对李先生进行了讯问，他承认在第二次来访时，义勇队员告知他其侄子的生命处于危险之中，但他们会尽力确保其获释。李先生随后表示，部分原因是因为自己由义勇队员安全护送至饭店，且基于他们承诺设法释放其侄子，他给了他们600.00美元。他们离开时向他保证，可能能够在次日（1932年2月1日）设法使其侄子获释。

进一步讯问结果显示，李先生及其侄子出生于缅甸并声称拥有英国国籍，但在1929年来到上海时，他们申领了中国护照，手中并无英国护照，也未在英国驻上海领事馆注册。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.

Central Station,

REPORT

Date January 29, 1932.

Subject (in full) Closing of shops in the Central District.

Made by D. S. I. Shields Forwarded by J. S. Colquhoun

Sir,

I beg to report that at 12:15 p.m. 29-1-32 C.D.C.s 37 and 261 reported to the undersigned that practically all the shops in Honan and Foochow Roads had closed their doors and pasted notices on same to the effect that they were declaring a General Strike in protest to the Japanese Invasion of Chinese Territory. These posters were issued by the Chamber of Commerce.

D. O. "A", C.D.I. Robertson of the Special Branch and C.D.I. Mason informed by telephone. No disturbance was caused through this action. Later it was ascertained that all shops in Honan Road and and all but six in Foochow Road are closed.

J. Shields.
D. S. I.

(Initials)
Senior Detective (Central)

4/2
H.R. 9/2.
D. O. "A"

报告

日期：1932年1月29日。

事由（全称）：中央区店铺关门停业。

制作人：侦探副督察希尔兹（Shields） 转呈人：J. S. Colquhoun

先生：

卑职谨此报告，1932年1月29日中午12时15分，中央捕房巡长37号和261号向卑职报告，河南路和福州路上的几乎所有店铺均已关门，并在门上张贴告示，宣称举行总罢工，以抗议日本入侵中国领土。这些海报由商会发布。

已通过电话通知“A”区值班官、特别支部刑事侦缉督察罗伯逊（Robertson）及刑事侦缉督察梅森（Mason）。此举未引发任何骚乱。后经查明，河南路所有店铺及福州路除六家外的所有店铺均已关闭。

J. 希尔兹。
侦探副督察。
